highlights.title: ‘Wellness is on the ballot’: Why did so many pilates studios tell me to vote in the midterms?
highlights.summary: Owners of pilates and yoga studios in the US got political and encouraged their followers to vote on social media. Your local pilates instructors only want you to do two things: breathe through your side-planks and vote.
body: In the days leading up to the US midterm elections, a wave of posts from fitness and wellness accounts blanketed Instagram, eschewing their typical messaging around the importance of strengthening your core in favor of the importance of exercising your civic duty. Owners of pilates and yoga studios and instructors across the US posted reels and pictures on platforms like Instagram encouraging their followers and clients to vote. Engagement varied depending on their following: posts reaped anywhere from 70 to more than 10,000 likes.
“A strong core is cute. Having a voice is powerful. Go vote,” posted Frederick Ocansey, a pilates instructor who goes by the name flyfreshfreddy on his Instagram account with nearly 25,000 followers.
“A pilates class no-show only costs you,” an Instagram reel posted by a Flatbush, Brooklyn studio KGC Pilates read. “An election no-show costs all of us.”
points: Owners of pilates and yoga studios in the US got political and encouraged their followers to vote on social media.
Your local pilates instructors only want you to do two things: breathe through your side-planks and vote.

highlights.title: The Results Are In: Voters Hate Data Centers
highlights.summary: From high-profile Senate races to local rezoning initiatives, data centers and their supporters did miserably on the ballot in the 2026 midterms.
body: It was a bad night for data centers. In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown, who has aired ads for months calling his opponent “the face of data centers in Ohio,” cruised to victory to flip a Senate seat. Democrat Chris Pappas, who when seated will be the nation’s first openly gay male senator, mentioned his opposition to data centers in his victory speech and drew massive boos from his crowd in New Hampshire—even though the state has no large-scale data centers under construction.
Elsewhere, two separate Republicans named Derek and Derrick, whose Democratic opponents labeled them “Data Center Derek” and “DC Derrick,” suffered losses in House races in Ohio and Wisconsin.

As part of last night’s shocking blue tsunami, voters selected candidates with tough policies on data centers at all levels of government, in a clear rebuke to the industry’s buildout in states across the country. Almost a quarter of all voters told NBC News that data centers were “crucial” to their vote, while nearly two-thirds said it was either a major or minor factor.

highlights.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell says he has full movement in his lower body after he was taken to hospital with a neck injury during Sunday's NFL win over the Minnesota Vikings.
body: Campbell was face down on the turf and not moving after hitting tight end TJ Hockenson early in the fourth quarter of the Lions' 19-15 victory on Sunday.
The 26-year-old was evaluated by medical personnel before being strapped to a board and carefully lifted onto the cart to a round of applause.
Detroit's entire team and most of the coaching staff surrounded the cart.
Campbell offered his own injury update on Wednesday, noting that he also has movement in his upper body.

highlights.title: PS Plus Makes James Bond’s New Game Free for Just One Hour
highlights.summary: 007 First Light starts with a bang. James Bond’s latest mission begins with a cold-open action sequence that segues into one of the best video game tutorials in recent memory. PlayStation Plus members can now try that impressive introduction for free.
body: Video game tutorials are famously Not Very Good. Many are dull introductions that over-explain every gameplay system in exhaustive detail instead of letting players put things together for themselves. Even in cinematic, story-focused games, pop-up menus clog the screen, making it impossible to get lost in the world.

A main difference with First Light ’s tutorial is that it happens in-universe. You come to learn how the game works alongside Bond’s in-universe training, as the neophyte spy learns the tools of the trade in a playable training montage that jump-cuts between different set pieces. There are car races, fistfights, and mock infiltration missions where Bond tries to earn his place in a program that virtually no one thinks he belongs in. The sequence is stylish and provides a narrative buy-in that most game tutorials don’t even attempt.

At least based on 007 First Light' s sales, it seems quite possible the game will get a sequel. After launching in May, 007 First Light had already sold an impressive 4 million copies by August, making it one of the best-selling games of 2026 so far.

highlights.title: Data centers lost the midterms
highlights.summary: Data center developers are poised to face a more restrictive building environment after voters across the country voted in candidates who favor moratoriums and ballot measures that put more obstacles on their expansion, delivering a stinging blow to a central pillar of the AI industry.
body: In ballot measures and exit polls, voters across the country rejected unrestrained development.

Of voters polled by NBC News on Election Day, 76 percent said they opposed data centers in their communities. Dozens of local communities voted directly to restrict development through ballot measures. And upset winners like Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and Michigan’s Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed support moratoriums on development.

It’s hard to draw a direct line from data center backlash to the election of any of these candidates, and there were still some races where candidates who favored more limited restrictions on data centers prevailed. Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who previously lauded development in Florida, was elected as governor, and Iowa’s Democratic Governor-elect Rob Sand opposed a moratorium that his challenger favored. But even these candidates were forced to engage on data center issues during their campaigns, and will be likely to face continued pressure to put at least some guardrails in place.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Sells Nearly 8 Million Copies Before It Even Launches, Report Says
highlights.summary: The anticipation surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 is reaching a fever pitch as Rockstar Games' long-awaited open-world adventure gets closer to its launch. Between fans dissecting every trailer, an alligator Xbox sweepstakes capitalizing on the hype, and players preparing their hard drives for the…
body: Now, new estimates suggest that the excitement is already translating into some seriously impressive sales figures. According to data from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has reportedly sold approximately 7.71 million copies ahead of its Nov. 19 release. That's translated to an estimated $751 million in revenue, despite not being available to play yet.

Sensor Tower's figures suggest that PlayStation accounts for 74% of those sales, with Xbox making up the remaining 26%. While Rockstar has yet to officially confirm its preorder numbers, the estimates offer an interesting glimpse into just how enormous the demand for GTA 6 has become.
To put those numbers into perspective, GTA 6 is already comfortably in the conversation among 2026's best-selling games, despite still being more than two weeks away from launch.

The latest year-to-date sales rankings from Circana offer a useful snapshot of the competition. Its current top ten includes major releases such as NBA 2K27, Resident Evil: Requiem, 007 First Light, MLB: The Show 26, Crimson Desert, and Call of Duty: Black Ops II.

highlights.summary: Tony, Grammy, and Emmy winner Cynthia Erivo has joined the cast of Universal’s upcoming Snoop Dogg biopic and is set to portray Tupac’s mother, Afeni Shakur. Jonathan Daviss stars in “Snoop,” which is described as the “definitive biopic of the entertainment mogul and icon,” Snoop Dogg.
body: Afeni Shakur — the late mother of rapper Tupac was a prominent member of the Black Panther Party.

Born in North Carolina as Alice Faye Williams in 1947, Afeni Shakur moved to the Bronx with her mother as an 11-year-old. She joined the Panthers after hearing Bobby Seale speak in 1968, and married fellow Black Panther member Lumumba Shakur soon after.

Craig Brewer (“Hustle and Flow,” “Song Sung Blue”) is directing “Snoop,” which Universal dated for theatrical release on Aug. 6, 2027, based on his rewrite of Joe Robert Cole’s (“Black Panther, “”Wakanda Forever”) original script.

Snoop Dogg is producing “Snoop,” which will incorporate music from his vast catalog, alongside Imagine Entertainment’s Brian Grazer (“8 Mile”) and Allan Mandelbaum and Death Row Pictures president Sara Ramaker. “Snoop” is the first project under Death Row Pictures’ overall deal with NBCUniversal Entertainment & Studios. Senior VP of production development Ryan Jones and director of development Tony Ducret will oversee the project for the studio.

highlights.title: Nothing teases a screen-free AI device ahead of launch next month
highlights.summary: Nothing CEO Carl Pei said in a post on X that the company's launching its first AI device in December. That's just a little over a year after Pei announced plans for "AI-native" devices and an AI operating system.
body: CEO Carl Pei says Nothing’s first ‘AI-native’ device ‘couldn’t have been an app.’

“Our first AI-native product ships next month. It’s a tool, but one built with the personality and care that have come to define a Nothing product. It has no new screen, and it couldn’t have been an app.”

Pei shared an image with the post that says “NOTHING(R)” in the top left corner, above an ambiguous black rounded corner. Last month, a rumor claimed Nothing is planning to launch two pairs of AI smart glasses, including one without cameras, and an earlier rumor said it’s “repositioning itself as an AI-first company” with a shift to AI accessories.

Nothing’s AI device wouldn’t be the first screen-free AI gadget, following the likes of the Humane AI pin, the Friend, and even AI stuffed animals. OpenAI is also reportedly working on an AI smart speaker with Jony Ive. Pei alluded to earlier AI devices, saying, “the whole industry is hunting for its iPhone moment: the pendant, the pin, the glasses, the companion, some magical consumer device that makes AI part of everyone’s life.” He added, “Looking for the iPhone of AI today is a dead end.”

highlights.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman spent election night defending his position on PC RAM purchases. He changed his name on X to "Ram Altman" in response to another user's comment, saying, "i actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is…
body: The OpenAI CEO rebranded to ‘Ram Altman’ on X, saying, ‘i want you to have so much ram.’
He replied to another comment, saying, “i want you to have so much ram lets build more.”

Altman’s posts follow an interview on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he said “it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.” AI data centers have been snapping up the world’s RAM supply, driving shortages that are leading to tech price hikes and making it tough for many people to “have so much ram” like Altman says he wants. The RAM shortage might not let up anytime soon, either — Intel’s expecting it to last through at least next year, and SK Hynix predicted it could drag on until 2030.

body: Meanwhile, fans have new material to feed their theories about The Elder Scrolls 6: a title, Sentinel, and a juicy quote from a Moth Priest. Since the game was announced in 2018, theories have proliferated (there’s nothing else we can do, after all!). Some have been proven true, some will quite likely be proven true, and some are just absurd, but we still would like to see them come to fruition.

Let’s start with an easy one. Speculation that Hammerfell will be the setting of the next game in the series began with the first teaser shown in 2018. The geography and environmental features pointed to the Redguards' homeland, and the Nov. 3 reveal confirmed it. Sentinel is a major city in Hammerfell, also present in The Elder Scrolls Online, and the quote shared with the teaser is attributed to a Moth Priest serving High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

highlights.title: Apple will check shared iCloud links for ‘harmful content’
highlights.summary: Apple will start checking iCloud items that are accessible to anyone who has the link for "harmful content" starting with iOS 27.3 and other 27.3 updates, the company says.
body: If you make an item on iCloud available to anyone who has the link, Apple will be able to check it starting with iOS 27.3.

“When you share an item that can be accessed by Anyone with the Link in version 27.3 or later of iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS, that content is made accessible to Apple to check for harmful content,” according to a support document reported on by 9to5Mac. Sharing something over iCloud with the “Anyone with the Link” permissions will also mean that it’s no longer end-to-end encrypted.
Apple’s support document does not define what “harmful content” is. But this new approach follows calls from protestors for Apple to crack down on child sexual abuse material stored in iCloud.

Apple says it “reserves the right to move, refuse, modify, remove, or delete” any harmful content that a user attempts to upload. Apple may also block or disable accounts, prevent a user from making a new account, or, “if necessary,” invoke law enforcement.

highlights.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
highlights.summary: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, expanding Codex’s tools for building, understanding, and reviewing code.
body: Today we're announcing that OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc ⁠ (opens in a new window). (“Pierre”), the company behind Code Storage ⁠ (opens in a new window) and a family of standout open-source developer tools. If you’ve browsed files or reviewed a change in the Codex app, you’ve already used Pierre’s Trees and Diffs libraries. We’re excited to work with the Pierre team to build on the Git workflows that developers already rely on and adapt them to how teams work with coding agents.

We’ve seen in our own engineering work how the systems around Git need to evolve as more of that work happens in parallel. Earlier this week, we shared how we’re scaling Git at OpenAI with Pando, our in-house source control backend for engineers and agents. With the Pierre team, we wish to set the standard for modern software development: from the first branch an agent creates to that magic moment when code is deployed to the world. body: A ndy Field was midway through his standup run at this year’s Edinburgh fringe when he was struck by an unusual urge – the urge to draw a horse. “I hadn’t sat down to draw anything since I was at school,” says the 34-year-old comedian. “Drawing was a skill I didn’t have.”

He’s not lying. The subsequent horse Field posted to TikTok and Instagram was rather naive, with its four identical straight legs and cartoon eyeball. But the project he announced alongside it – Drawing a Horse Every Day Until I’m Really Good at Drawing Horses – immediately captured people’s hearts. Over a million people watched the minute-long video of him drawing that first horse with a four-colour ballpoint pen. By day three – an undeniably terrible effort in which the horse appeared to have sprouted a platypus’s bill – more than two million, by his estimation, had tuned in. “People were willing the series to continue,” says Field. And so he did.

highlights.title: The Lawyer Holding Big Tech Accountable by ‘Beating the Tar Out of Them’ in Court
highlights.summary: Mark Lanier led the first social media addiction case to go to trial, winning a verdict against Meta and Google in March. It’s just the beginning.
body: As social media giants face allegations that they fail to protect users, attorney Mark Lanier is grappling with the question: What would it actually take to hold companies accountable?
"I think it just takes beating the tar out of them," Lanier told WIRED senior correspondent Lauren Goode at the WIRED World Fair on Wednesday.

Lanier was the lead attorney in the first social media addiction case to go to trial, which resulted in a verdict against Meta and Google in March. The plaintiff was awarded $6 million in damages —a symbolic victory, but a rounding error in terms of the tech giants’ bottom lines.

Lanier said lawsuits in which attorneys general represent their states have the potential to orchestrate significant change, alongside greater financial repercussions. In a case that went to trial in August, attorneys general across several states—including Arkansas, where Lanier’s firm served as outside counsel—accused Meta of failing to protect young social media users.

highlights.title: UK Officials Said AI Would Add £400 Billion to the Economy. That Figure Mainly Came From Google
highlights.summary: The AI minister now concedes the estimated figure is less than a third of that. Researchers blame the country’s slow rate of adoption.
body: For the last two years, the UK government has been telling the British public that the country could receive an economic boost of £400 billion ($538 billion), thanks to AI, a figure intended to calm fears that the technology would lead to sweeping job losses and even an economic crash.

But the UK AI minister admitted last week that figure was significantly higher than the government’s actual projections after it was revealed that the assessment came solely from a report commissioned by Google and that its own estimation of AI’s economic benefit was less than a third of that £400 billion figure.

AI minister Kanishka Narayan, answering a parliamentary question on the issue, said that AI adoption and data investment could add £55 billion to £140 billion to the UK economy by 2030, bringing the central estimate to £120 billion. But even this “more recent assessment,” he said, was a “hugely uncertain” estimate.
Narayan said the £400 billion figure “was drawn from a publicly available 2023 report commissioned by Google and produced by Public First,” a British consultancy firm now referred to as PF Global.

highlights.title: After Martha Stewart’s Halloween homeless costume disaster, I have to know: celebrities, why do you risk it? | Coco Khan
highlights.summary: Cynics might say it’s about courting controversy, but I think these fancy dress faux-pas hint at a bleaker truth. It’s not easy being an optimist these days. It requires practice, like exercising a muscle.
body: And so it is that this week I find my optimism being put through its paces by the news of US superstar homemaker Martha Stewart and her offensive Halloween costume of a homeless person, complete with a dirt-smeared face and a sign reading “I AM HUNGRY HELP ME!!”.

How’s this for a more upbeat interpretation: she is preparing for her next chapter as an edgy, anti-humour one-woman act known as Martha Stewart Lee. I can see it now: her Fringe show – which I am calling Laundered – receiving rave reviews. “After decades of perfect tablescapes, Martha Stewart serves up something truly unpalatable: herself.” Five stars!

Before influencers made “being a Pinterest board made flesh” a viable career, there was Stewart. Arguably the US’s national authority on doing domestic things properly, Stewart, now 85, built an empire of cookbooks, magazines, TV shows and homeware. In 1999, she took her company public and became a billionaire. Then, in 2004, she was convicted of conspiracy, obstruction of an agency proceeding and making false statements to federal investigators, and served five months in prison.

highlights.title: Trump’s billionaire-blue collar coalition has been smashed by class politics | Aditya Chakrabortty
highlights.summary: As tech bosses get richer and ordinary Americans struggle, Democrats put the case against the US’s grotesque unfairness – and voters responded. Remember the “vibe shift”?
body: Remember the “vibe shift”? Just last year, columnists and corporate boardrooms alike declared that the second coming of Donald Trump meant the old rules of politics and even everyday civility were roadkill.
“I feel liberated,” one top banker told the Financial Times. “We can say ‘retard’ and ‘pussy’ without the fear of getting cancelled … it’s a new dawn.”

Silicon Valley, Wall Street and east coast media owners all saw Trumpism not as a political strategy but as a turn in the entire culture: a vibe shift to the right. They were wrong. Tuesday night was a comprehensive rejection of the president. Before the midterms, ultra-wealthy donors such as Musk poured billions into Trump’s proxies, but the working- and middle-class base were not having it. The relatively new coalition that put the orange man in the White House has been smashed apart by old-fashioned class politics.

Among Mamdani’s achievements has been his reminder to ordinary voters that when they can’t afford the basics, it’s not just because prices are unreasonably high – it’s also because their pay is unfairly low. He has tied the cost of living to an argument about inequality, and rightly so.

body: The 26-year-old was treated for nine minutes on the field after making a tackle during Sunday’s game. Players from both teams were visibly distraught as Campbell received medical attention before he was taken for further treatment at a hospital in the Detroit area.

In a statement on Wednesday, Campbell said he is making progress in his recovery. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” Campbell, who remains hospitalized, said in the statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.”
On Monday, Lions coach Dan Campbell paid tribute to the former first-round pick’s contributions to the team.

highlights.title: ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?
highlights.summary: It’s 20 years since Jo and Richard Hill bought anything in Rotherham town centre. Why have they and so many locals abandoned it for the nearest retail park – and what would it take to change their minds? On 22 May 1987, retail history was made in Rotherham.
body: Almost 40 years on, the razzle is a bit less dazzling. Parkgate, as the retail park is called now, looks like any large big-box outdoor shopping centre you might find on urban fringes. There’s a Primark, a Sports Direct and a Matalan, plus (of course) a Frankie & Benny’s. Shoppers still seem to love it. “I think it’s ideal. It’s got everything here,” says Robert Gordon. The 66-year-old retired factory production manager had popped to Pets at Home to get a cupcake and toy for his dog Bruno’s fourth birthday.

Gordon has lived in Rotherham for 24 years. “A lot of people come to outlets like this. It’s very rare we go into the town centre and, if we did, we’d go to Sheffield,” he says. He is hardly an outlier. Almost half of Britons don’t visit their high street weekly. Instead, shoppers are opting for retail parks. Business is so strong, retailers are scrambling for spots, even paying extra to secure their place. By the end of 2025, only 4.8% of retail park lots in Britain were vacant, according to real estate consultancy Knight Frank – the lowest level on record. Vacancy rates for UK high streets, on the other hand, sit at 13%, reports Savills.

Why have they and so many locals abandoned it for the nearest retail park – and what would it take to change their minds?

videos.title: RE-𝙇𝙄𝙑𝙀 Summer Youth Olympics! Men's Street Skateboarding Heats 1 & 2 | #Dakar2026
body: Dakar 2026 is officially making history as the first Olympic event ever hosted in Africa! From October 31st – November 13th, 2026, Senegal will host 2,700 athletes and 207 delegations across 25 competitive sports and 10 engagement sports.
“Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates” — get ready for an unforgettable Youth Olympic Games!
